rows.en: Maybe it really was just a dream after all.{p}

The gathering I went to because Hino, my senior in the newspaper club, asked me to.
The six who gathered there vanished one by one, each time a story was told.{p}

And when all six had vanished, the masked girl appeared.
She hinted that the six were dead, and then she too vanished from before my eyes.{p}

I was a person named {b} {a}.
And I was a first-year at this school.{p}

And I was a member of the newspaper club, and Hino was there too.
And so I confirmed that the world I was in now was reality.
But one thing was different.
Just one thing was different from the reality I knew.{p}

It was that the newspaper club's plan to do a feature on the seven wonders had never existed in the first place.
Naturally, when I brought it up, Hino tilted his head with a puzzled look.
Akemi Iwashita.
Nozomu Kazama.
Makoto Shindo.
Tomoharu Hosoda.
Shoji Arai.
Reiko Fukuzawa.
Hino didn't know a single one of their names.
I checked the school roster.
But there wasn't a single student by any of those names.
Thinking I might have missed them, I checked again and again.
But it was wasted effort.
They didn't exist.
They were never students who belonged at this school.{p}

...Then what was it that I saw?
What had that gathering been in the first place?
Had I been daydreaming?
A terribly realistic dream?{p}

No, that was no dream.
Those six were undeniably there, laughing, breathing.
Even now I remember them so clearly that I could tell each of them apart by their faces, their laughter, even their scent.
The seven of us, who met and shared one fleeting moment in such a short time.
They exist.
I'm certain of it, and yet I go on living the same old everyday life, unable to clear away the thing lodged in my chest.
...And today, that old school building is being torn down.
The first term had ended, and it was already summer vacation.
What should I do?
Should I go to the school?{p}And see the old school building being torn down?
Go to the school
Don't go to the school
I could hear the noise of the construction from quite far away.{p}

...They're already tearing down the old school building.
I ran.
Just as I reached the school, the old building was coming down with a roar.
It was almost as if it had been waiting for me to arrive.
I staggered toward the old building as if I were being lured.
"It's dangerous, move aside."{p}One of the construction workers urged me to keep my distance.
Say you're covering it for the newspaper club
Move away as you're told
Ignore the warning and go closer

"Um, I'm with the newspaper club.
And, well, I was told to cover the demolition of the old school building..."
"Nobody told me about that."
The worker looked troubled and folded both arms.
"...Well, fine. Just don't get in the way."
At that, I bowed.
I approached the flattened wreckage of the old school building.
Now that it had come to this, there was no trace left of the old building, frightening as it had been, yet full of character.
It was nothing but a heap of garbage.{p}

"Heeeeey! A body! There's a body here!☆"
A loud voice rang out not far away.
Maybe somewhere in my heart I had been expecting that.
Amid the stirring crowd, I held back my eagerness and headed for the spot where the voice had come from too.
"...This poor soul hasn't been dead long."
"Ain't this a student from this school?"
"One... two... three... there's six of 'em!"
Everyone surrounded the bodies, gazing at them with deeply sympathetic eyes.{p}

There were six bodies in school uniforms.
Four were male.
Two were female.
They lay buried in the ruins of the rubble, piled on top of one another.
Every one of the bodies was pristine.
Perhaps because they lay face down, their faces couldn't be seen.
But I knew who they were.
I didn't need to look at their faces; I knew very well whose bodies these were.{p}

"Call the police!"
Someone shouted.
Then another voice rose from farther off.
"There's bones over here! There's a whole lotta skeletons buried here!"
"What the hell kind of school is this..."
People's voices flew back and forth, half appalled, half astonished.
Just how many human lives had this old school building devoured until now?{p}

In any case, those six had really existed.
Inside the old school building, at least, they had existed.
Their identities would surely never be confirmed.
But they had definitely been there.
If I'm in the real world now, that is...
The weight in my chest finally lifted, so I decided to head home.{p}

In the old school building, left unused for so long, residents of some unknowable world must have settled in.
And in that place they are born, they live, and they die.
Living inside the old school building, they must have known it would soon be destroyed.
And so, wanting to tell me something, they must have shown me those visions.
I must have had that strange experience because I was bewitched by the people who live in the old school building.{p}

...That was the thought that suddenly came to me.
Am I wrong to think so?
Or has my mind just gone strange, and I'm only seeing hallucinations?
Is the masked girl nothing but a figment of my own imagination?{p}
...The night had grown late.{p}What should I do?
Go to sleep now
Read a book
Maybe do some studying

I opened the drawer to take out something to write with.
In there was...{p}

That mask.
The mask lay carefully in the middle of the drawer, as if someone had placed it there.
The mask that had disappeared when I left the old school building.
It was here, in the drawer of the study desk in my own house.{p}What could it mean, that mask being here?
I'm being invited too
A gift from that girl
I'm still dreaming
Am I being invited?{p}

I picked up the mask.
The instant I did, I felt as though I had touched something I should never have touched.
What was it that had been in the old school building?
Where will the things that were in the old school building go now?{p}

Without realizing it, I held the mask up to my face.
The moment it touched, I felt dizzy for an instant, and my view changed completely.{p}

The scene I saw through the mask.
It was the old school building.
And standing in front of me was me.
This place is... isn't this the girls' restroom in the old school building?
To me in the mask, the me in front of me said just one thing.
"I don't want to see."{p}

...I see.
You don't want to see my face?
Then don't look.
At your own face.
I'm still in the nightmare.
In a pleasant nightmare.{p}

Forget it.
What good would it do to see something like that now?{p}

I flopped down on my bed.
It's always like this lately.
Did something inside me vanish along with those six?
I can't bring myself to do anything.
I let out a deep sigh.
...Heh.{p}
What?
I definitely heard something just now.{p}

I looked around the room.
Is someone there★
All I could see was my room, the same as always.
But that presence just now...
Heh heh...{p}

There it is again!
There really is someone in this room besides me.{p}

"Wh... Who's there?"
My voice cracked.
Whoever it was, their laughter grew louder.
And it was a voice I knew.
"How cold of you. Have you forgotten me already?"{p}

"Oh, but you can hear it, see?"
Just then, the owner of the mischievous voice appeared.
Suddenly, as if pulling open an invisible curtain.
I stared at her, unable to believe it.{p}

"Fu... kuzawa..."
The one standing before me was Reiko Fukuzawa.
"What's with that face? Like you've seen a ghost or something."
Even if she says that...
She vanished right in front of me.
She wasn't even on the roster.
Even just now, she appeared out of nowhere.
If she's not a ghost, then what exactly does she mean to say she is?{p}

"Shindo★"
At some point, Shindo had sat himself down on my desk.{p}

"You think nothing can exist in this world except what you can understand, don't you?"
In the chair beside him sat Hosoda.{p}
"Oh my, but I don't dislike that side of you."{p}
"Yes, it just goes to show how earnest you are, {a}."{p}

Iwashita, Arai, and even Kazama.
"N... No way..."
I rubbed my eyes without thinking.
Kazama shrugged.
"Hey now, you're not going to call a dashing, ultra-handsome heartthrob like me a hallucination, are you?"
The way he said it took away any urge to talk back.
No doubt about it, this was Kazama.{p}
Then the others too?{p}

"Looks like you finally get it. It was us who told you about the seven wonders the other day."
Fukuzawa smiled sweetly.
"H-How..."
I murmured without thinking.{p}

But I wasn't really sure myself what I was asking.
There were so many things I wanted to ask.{p}

Were all those stories lies?
Why did you vanish like that?
How did you get into the room without opening the door?
And above all, what are you?
...But they didn't seem to have any intention of answering any of it.{p}

"I'm sorry we startled you. You see, that was a test."
Arai said it with a cheerful smile.
A test?
"Yes. To see whether you were fit to be one of us."{p}

"And you passed. Simple as that."
Laughing warmly, they all came closer to me.{p}
"O... one of you... Doesn't that mean you're ghosts?"{p}

Hosoda snorted at my words.
"Still on about that? Listen, we live in the school. We never grow old, so we can watch over that school forever."{p}
"You're inside a long dream. If you become one of us, you'll never have to go back to ugly reality."{p}
"It hardly ever happens that someone gets chosen to join us, you know. It's been about ten years since the last time."{p}

That long?
Weren't these people human?{p}
I looked up at the smiles in front of me.{p}
"Even when we vanished one by one, you tried to keep the stories going. We liked that nerve of yours."{p}
"And the cool head to switch gears right away, even though I nearly killed you."{p}
"When it was my turn, I thought you'd call the police too, but you didn't, did you?"{p}

"Put all that together, and you've passed. Thrilled, aren't you?"
"Huh..."{p}

That wasn't what I'd meant to do at all.
It would be more accurate to say I'd been stunned by how many things kept happening.
In the end, maybe it meant I'd silently allowed everyone to vanish.
But it wasn't as if I'd meant to do that from the start......
...No, was that true?
Somewhere in my heart, hadn't I been thinking that if people really vanished, it would make a good article?{p}
I looked deep into my own heart.{p}And the heart I saw there was...
I was hoping everyone would vanish
Absolutely not, I never thought that

That's right.
I'd been thinking it would be fine if all six of them just disappeared.
For no other reason than that it would make a more interesting article.
I had never noticed until now, but inside me there was an evil darkness.
Maybe that was what had drawn the six of them to me.{p}

They held out their hands to me.
"Finally figured it out, have you? Well then, shall we go?"
I took their hands without hesitation.
The space behind them wavered softly.
The shimmering air, like a screen, showed a dark, black building.{p}

That's... the old school building.
"That's our world. And from now on, it will be your world too."
Without any resistance, my feet rose off the ground.
I would pass through the screen and go there.
To my new world.
Yes, now I understood.
The calm, lovely atmosphere of the old school building.
The masked girl had to be there too.
Somehow, I longed desperately to see her.
Pressing a hand to my fluttering heart, I plunged into that world, shimmering like a heat haze.{p}

No.
I absolutely never thought anything like that.{p}

"Tell me about it. Guess there's no way you're joining us after all."
Shindo shrugged.{p}
"That kind of killed the mood. Let's go home."{p}
"Yes, let's."{p}

They all turned their backs on me.
"Ah, w... wait a minute!"{p}

Kazama turned around.
"{a}, you've failed. You have no right to come with us. Go on, wake up from your dream."
A dream... he said?
Could I escape from the nightmare that had gone on and on?
Maybe hope showed on my face.{p}

Seeing me like that, Kazama raised his eyebrows in plain contempt.
"...How foolish."
"Huh?"
What did he just...?{p}

By the time I tried to ask him again, the six of them had vanished.
And then I realized.
At some point, I had come to be floating in a pitch-black void.
What is this★
I was supposed to be in my own room.
As far as I could see, there was nothing.
An absolute darkness that seemed to swallow even light.
Where am I?
Why am I in a place like this★
"Somebody...!"
I tried shouting, and a chill ran through me.
It felt as if my voice was being sucked into infinite space.
"Heh heh heh... What are you making such a fuss about?"
A woman's voice spoke inside my head.
"You were the one who refused to come to us... who wished to wake from the dream..."
No!
So this was reality?
An endless darkness with nothing in it at all.
Not just the seven wonders feature, but the school and my room too, were they all products of a dream?
No, even more than that...{p}

"That's right. Your name isn't {b} {a}. No such person ever existed in the first place..."
The voice echoing in my head told me the truth, calmly and cruelly.
I see... I remember now.
This is the masked girl's voice.
"You woke from the dream, just as you wished. Now you'll wander forever in this infinite reality."
"Wa..."
I tried to say, "Wait."
But no voice came out.
How was I supposed to face this heavy, crushing reality from now on?
...No answer came back anymore.

I began to fall slowly toward the center of the darkness.
I understood.
That I would never dream again.{p}

"All right..."
Nodding weakly, I moved away from there.{p}
Turning my back on the old school building, I looked toward the school gate.{p}

There was a schoolgirl there, even though it was summer vacation.
Had she come to see the old school building before it was torn down, like me?
But even so, something about her was strange.
I couldn't say exactly what...{p}

I hurried to catch up with her.
"Hey, you!"{p}

...The face that turned toward me wore a pure white mask.
It was that girl!
As I stood there, unable to breathe, the eyes beneath the mask seemed to smile faintly.
"So you came after all."
Her manner said she had seen it all coming.
"You look like you're wondering how I knew. If you want to know, shall I show you?"{p}

The girl took a small mirror out of her breast pocket.
Then she thrust it right in front of my eyes.
"Look..."
At her urging, I peered into the mirror.{p}

Reflected there was the same mask the girl wore.
I hurriedly put my hand to my face.
It felt hard and cold.
Is this... a mask?
When did I put on a mask★
I don't remember doing it.
No, I'm not wearing one.
But then, what on earth...?{p}

"Don't you understand?"
Her icy voice held my panic down.
"That mask is yours. After all, I am you..."
"That's..."
There was no way something so absurd could be true.{p}

I knocked her hand away.
The mirror hit the ground and shattered.
"I don't believe it! I'm me☆"
I grabbed the mask with both hands and tore it off with all my strength.
The mask came away without any resistance at all.{p}

But the girl pointed at my face.
"Then who is that supposed to be?"{p}

"Heh heh heh... It's no use."
The girl laughed.
The scattered mirror shards floated up, drifting lightly.
"Take a look. Who do you see in them?"{p}

The shards surrounded me.
Each tiny mirror caught my reflection.
But the one reflected there wasn't me.
Arai was there.
Iwashita, and Kazama too.
Shindo was laughing.
And even Hosoda and Fukuzawa.
All of them were looking at me from inside the mirrors.{p}

It's a lie.
This can't be...{p}

"Th... then... who am I?"
The girl answered my hoarse voice with a question.
"Did you think your body belonged to you alone?"
At that moment, a terrible headache struck me.
I couldn't help crouching down.{p}

...I don't know how long I stayed like that.
"Heeeeey! A body! There's a body here☆"
A loud shout went up from the direction of the old school building.
"...This one's only just died."
"Ain't this a student from this school?"
"One... two... three... There's seven of 'em!"
I caught broken snatches of talk like that too.{p}

I didn't need to look to know whose bodies they were.
They were my bodies.
I had something far more important to do than that.
That's right, I had to write up the call for storytellers.
When summer vacation was over, I would look for people to tell me the school's seven wonders.
Seven people to tell me the most terrifying stories of all.
Of course, I intend to treat them with the utmost courtesy.
After all, they might be me as well.{p}

Ignoring that voice, I kept walking closer and closer.
As if something were calling me...{p}

"..............................!"
...Someone seemed to be saying something, but it didn't reach my ears.
I kept going, closer and closer to the old school building, now a heap of rubble.
And before I knew it, I had walked right into the middle of the rubble.
"{a}!"
I heard someone call my name and spun around.
Why, the six of them were standing over there!
I ran toward them in a rush.{p}

What were they doing in a place like this?
I kept running, that question in my mind.
So what happened that day hadn't been a dream after all?
No, maybe the six of them standing there was itself a dream.{p}
"Look out☆"{p}

...Where am I?
I was floating gently in a lazy, drifting doze.
...Huh?
What happened after that...?
Oh, right.
I went to see the old school building, and I met those six.
And then...
Something hit my head with a tremendous impact...{p}

Oh, I see.
That's why I collapsed.
Which means this is the afterlife?
Have I died...?
...What an abrupt end that was.
I found I could accept my own death surprisingly calmly.
...Back then, those six were standing at the old school building, weren't they?
Did they call me to them?
If this really is the afterlife, they should be here too.
But it doesn't look like anyone's here but me.
It happened the instant I thought that.{p}

"{a}. So you made it."
It was a voice I knew well.
"Hosoda!"
I looked around for Hosoda.
But I couldn't see him anywhere.
"Hosoda! Hosoda!"
I called Hosoda's name with all my might, searching for him.
"Hey, {a}. Where are you looking?
I'm right here. And everyone else is with me, too."
I ran frantically toward the voice, but there was still no sign of Hosoda and the others.
"Where are you, Hosoda☆"{p}

Suddenly I felt uneasy.
It was as if I'd been left all alone in this vast, empty space.
Was I going to have to spend an endless stretch of time from now on, all alone, in a place with nothing at all?
Tears slowly welled up in my eyes.{p}What should I do...?
Head toward where the voice came from
Turn back

I headed in the direction Hosoda's voice had come from.
I couldn't think of anything else to do.
I pushed on through the empty space, relying on nothing but my instincts.
I thought I was heading toward the voice, but I began to worry whether this was really the right direction.
"Hosoda! ...Shindo!"
I ran on, calling out the names of those six.
But I couldn't hear Hosoda's voice anymore.{p}

Exhausted, I sank to the ground right where I was.
"...What am I supposed to do now?
Where am I supposed to go...?"
At a total loss, I broke down in tears.
"Hey, {a}! What are you crying for?
Jeez, you're one sniveling little sissy."
I heard Shindo's voice.
"You don't need to worry. You're going the right way.
You'll reach us soon.
Look, you can see us now, can't you?"
I looked toward where the voice had come from.
"Ah, everyone..."
Off in the distance, I could see those six standing there.
Suddenly my strength came back.
Forgetting how tired I had been, I started running toward them.
A little farther on, a small stream blocked my way, but I didn't care. I leapt right over it in one bound and kept going.{p}

"Yo, {a}. Glad you made it.
From now on, we're together forever.
Let's get along, huh?"
Shindo was in a great mood, too.{p}
The rest of them gave me a warm welcome as well.{p}

At this rate, it looked like I could live a happy life from here on.
...Though it's a little strange to talk about a 'life' after you've died.{p}

"Still, you came over to this world without the slightest hesitation, didn't you?
Even I threw quite a tantrum when it was time to cross that river.
Though in the end, I had no choice but to cross over to this side..."
Iwashita remarked.{p}

(Huh? That river...?)
I turned and looked behind me.{p}

"What?!"
I was stunned.
A moment ago it had been just a little stream, but now it had become a huge river.
And where I'd thought there was only empty space, I could now see the town where I had lived all this time.{p}

"...The Sanzu River..."
Could they mean the river flowing right in front of me?
Maybe, seen from the other side, this river looked no bigger than a little stream.
And I had gone and jumped right over that stream.
If I had turned back back then...
But now the great river blocked the way, and turning back was no longer possible.{p}
returns: 46:6038: RETURN - 'If I had turned back back then...' reads as a doubled word; editorial should rephrase ('at that moment').

rows.en:
"I like this world better.
I mean, it looks like it's gonna be fun from now on.
And {a} came too..."
Fukuzawa said, her voice bouncing with excitement.{p}

"That's right.
The other world was way too boring for me, too.
Everyone there was so hardheaded, they just couldn't keep up with my sense of style."
Kazama seemed to like this world, too.{p}

That's right. I couldn't turn back now anyway, so there was no use moping about it.
Instead of wishing I could go back, I should just enjoy my life here.{p}

Huh...?
What did Shindo just say?{p}

...Wait a minute.
Why should I have to be bullied out in the open?
Everyone was looking at me and smirking.
It was as if they'd found some tasty prey and were delighted.{p}

Terrified, I ran for my life.
"Hey, hey, you came to the world you wished for yourself, and now you're running away?"
Everyone surrounded me.
There was no escape anymore.
"I never wished for a world like this!
When I came to, I was just here.
...Besides, if this were really the world I wished for, you people wouldn't be here!"
I summoned my nerve and flung the words at them.
".............................."
Everyone fell silent.{p}

"...{a}, it's true that you wished for this world.
When people die, they go to the world they want most.
And of course, {a}, you're no exception.
Even if your head says you hate it, deep down in your mind, a world like this is what you want.
Everyone here was summoned by your mind, too.
{a}, you wished for a world where you'd get to be bullied by us, that's all."{p}

"No... no... nooooooo☆"
I screamed.
I didn't want to believe it.
That I could want a world like this.
That I could want those six to bully me.

How many hundreds of times did I repeat that?
Was this really the world I had wished for, after all?
And did I really want to be bullied by those six?
Maybe that was why, no matter how many times I ran, I always ended up back where those six were.{p}

I no longer had the strength to keep running.
As if they had been waiting for exactly that, those six came toward me, grinning from ear to ear.{p}

"Well, {a}. Got that out of your system?
Now it's your turn to play with us."
Shindo slung his arm around my shoulders, all chummy.
On his face was that white mask.{p}

I decided to turn back.
No matter how far I went, I didn't feel like I'd ever reach Hosoda and the others.
Besides, I had a feeling that someone was calling me from somewhere behind me, too.
"{a}! {a}! Where are you going?
Not that way. Come back here!"
Hosoda was calling out to me desperately.
But I shook off his voice and went back the way I had come.{p}

Hah, hah, hah...
How far back had I come?
Maybe I had long since passed the place where I started.
Even so, things didn't get any better.
The only difference was that I couldn't hear Hosoda's voice anymore.{p}

(...Maybe turning back was a mistake.
If I had kept going, maybe I could have reached Hosoda and the others...)
But I just couldn't bring myself to go any farther than that.
I didn't know why, but I couldn't stop feeling drawn to this direction.
But maybe that had just been my imagination, too.{p}

"...Who's there? Where are you?"
I looked all around, but there didn't seem to be anyone.
(Not again...)
It was the very moment I thought that.{p}

The masked woman appeared in front of me.
"Y-You're..."
I ran up to her so I wouldn't lose sight of her.
She waited for me.
I went up beside her and asked.
"Why are you here?
...And where is this place?
Am I dead?"
Then she answered.{p}

"I can't answer when you ask me so much at once.
...Well, fine.
I'll tell you.
First, your first question: I'm here because I came to stop you.
Your second question: this place is... let's see, what people call the border between this world and the next, I suppose.
And your last question.
You're still alive.
In pretty bad shape, though.
You're right on the edge between life and death.
Whether you make it or not is up to you."{p}

Hearing that, I suddenly didn't want to die anymore.
Until a moment ago I'd thought I was dead, and yet I was still alive.{p}

"{a}, if you'd kept going the way you were, you'd have died for certain.
Because those six were calling you.
I was calling you desperately too, but it seems you couldn't hear me.
But don't relax yet.
There's still a chance you could die.
If anything, the chance that you'll die is higher."
"What should I do?!
I don't want to die yet.
I want to keep on living!"
I pleaded with the masked woman.
"All right, I'll tell you.
Your body is badly injured, and on top of that, it has lost its soul.
That's why it keeps growing weaker and weaker.
If you go back to your body right now, your chances of being saved will go up."{p}

"...But how...?"{p}"You just need to make a way out of here.
This is a world inside your heart.
Something like a dream.
If you wish for it, the exit will open.
...But listen.
On the way back, there will be terrible suffering.
You might even think it would have been better not to go back.
At least be ready for that.
If you're not, the suffering may be more than you can bear.
And if you can't bear it, this time even your soul may be torn apart.
If that happens, you yourself will vanish.
No matter how you struggle, you'll never be able to come back again."{p}

As soon as she had said that much, she vanished all of a sudden, just as she had appeared.
At once I wished for an exit out of here to open.
Right in front of me, near where the masked woman had been standing, a small hole gaped open.
The harder I wished to return to my world, the wider the hole opened.
When it had opened wide enough for a person to pass through, I hurriedly leapt into the hole.{p}

"Waaaaaaaaah☆"
It felt like I was plummeting from a great height.
And I kept falling faster and faster.
I felt like I was about to black out.
I was falling headfirst through pitch-black space.{p}

Now and then, I could see bluish-white lights flitting here and there.
"What are those lights?"
To find out what they were, I followed one that streaked past close by with my eyes.
But soon there was no need.
The light came toward me on its own.{p}
"Whoa!"{p}

That ball of light had a face.
A bitter, resentful face...
The ball of light slammed into me.
With a tremendous shock, an image came flooding into me.{p}
...An image of a man I didn't know trying to kill me.{p}

The man plunged the kitchen knife he was holding into my stomach.
(It hurts☆)
A burning pain shot through me.
Hot blood poured out, and I could tell I was surely heading toward death.{p}
Another ball of light crashed into me.

...A rope tied in a loop hung before my eyes.
I stuck my head through it and jumped off the stool.

"Gkh..."
The rope tightened around my neck, and I couldn't breathe.{p}

The events that had led this person to attempt suicide surfaced in my mind.
Huge debts... a wife's betrayal.
Driven further and further into a corner mentally, the person finally thought of suicide.
(Are these balls of light the souls of people who died with bitter regrets and can't pass on...?){p}
Images like these flowed into me one after another.{p}

"...Please... no more..........."
My mind was on the verge of being torn apart.
...So this was the suffering she had talked about.
I desperately held together my mind, which felt about to scatter into pieces.{p}

..............................
...By now... how much time... has passed...?
My mind was in tatters, and I began to feel like nothing mattered anymore.
It was the very moment I thought I was finished.
I felt as if I had been caught, softly and gently.{p}

And then, with a feeling like waking from a dream, I opened my eyes.
I had come back to my own world.{p}

"Ow!"
A splitting pain shot through my head, and I came fully awake all at once.
"{b}! {b}☆"
There was my mother, pale-faced, looking at me with worry.
Behind her, my father was standing, too.
Now that I had woken up, the nurses around me started moving about in a hurry.{p}

I was in the intensive care unit.
My head was wrapped round and round in bandages.
At the construction site of the old school building, a piece of lumber falling from above had struck me square on the head, and I had been rushed to the hospital.
Apparently, after my surgery, I had been unconscious for days.
My condition had been bad the whole time, but just a little while ago I had become critical, and my father and mother had been called in.
According to the construction workers' testimony, I had walked into the rubble of the demolished old school building as if I were possessed.
And then, by bad luck, I had been pinned under lumber that came crashing down.
At the time, I had walked over toward those six because they were standing there.
But according to the people who saw it, there had been no one at that spot except the construction crew.{p}

But I had definitely seen those six standing there.
And I had heard the voice calling me, too.
Had I just been seeing things?
No, those had to be the ghosts of those six.
They must have been trying to take me with them.
Getting pinned under the lumber was no accident, either. Those six had set it up.
...I had very nearly been taken away by those six.
If I hadn't turned back at that moment...
And if the masked woman hadn't saved me, I would never have been able to regain consciousness like this.{p}

I had suffered a serious injury, a depressed skull fracture, but somehow I had managed not to die.
It would still be quite a while before I was discharged, but when that day came, I meant to write all of this up as a newspaper article no matter what.
The scary-stories feature itself had never existed.
If that was how it was, then I could just plan a new feature, couldn't I?
I'd make it a truly interesting article, without fail.
I was confident I could, and I had surely been through enough to write an interesting article.
Gazing out the window, I made that vow.{p}
